title: EU gas supplier displacement: bounded attribution tests and counterfactual gaps
scope: EU natural gas imports, all sources and modes, 2021 and 2025
units: billion cubic metres (bcm) unless otherwise indicated
denominatorWarning: Selected supplier shares are shares of Russia+US+Norway only, NOT shares of all EU gas imports; other suppliers omitted.

attributionTests.reason: All three suppliers in one EU gas source series; Russia 2021 approximate
All-gas imports in bcm, not LNG-only

attributionTests.test: US growth smaller than Russian loss
attributionTests.reason: 56.7 bcm increase versus 117 bcm Russian decline
Other suppliers, EU gas demand reduction, re-exports and portfolio rebalancing
DOE averages are not reconciled to invoices

attributionTests.test: Incremental company operating margin from Europe
attributionTests.reason: SEC consolidated results not segmented by EU destination
No project-level cost of capital matched to incremental European cargoes
Supply resilience and alternative sourcing not quantified
Gross fossil export revenue does not equal tax receipts or profit
No valid control or causal identification strategy
No readiness or influence score assigned

alternativeExplanations: Norway and other suppliers gained or maintained share
U.S. LNG export facilities ramped up capacity independently of EU sanctions
Global price changes and destination switching affect trade flows
Russian volumes shifted toward other markets
claimsAllowed: EU Russian gas imports declined substantially 2021–2025
EU U.S. gas imports increased substantially 2021–2025

claimsProhibited: 56.7 bcm of U.S. gas directly replaced Russian molecules
